Prediction Errors of Fitted Regression Models

Source: R/regressionMetrics.R
regression-metrics.Rd

Methods of the prediction error measures of DescToolsX for fitted models: the mean absolute error (DescToolsX::mae()), the mean squared error (DescToolsX::mse()) and its root (DescToolsX::rmse()), and the mean absolute percentage error, plain (DescToolsX::mape()) and symmetric (DescToolsX::smape()). The measures themselves work on predictions and observed values; the methods here take both from a model.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
mae(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
mse(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
rmse(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
mape(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'FitMod'
smape(x, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
mae(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
mse(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
rmse(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
mape(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
smape(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a regression model fitted with fitMod(), or an lm (incl. glm) object

newdata

an optional data frame to evaluate, containing the response. NULL (default) uses the training data. For models fitted with fitMod() only.

...

further arguments passed to the measure, e.g. na.rm

Value

As the respective measure in DescToolsX.

Details

For a model fitted with fitMod() the predictions come from predict.FitMod() on the response scale, so the methods work alike for every regression engine (linear, generalised linear, robust, trees, random forests, ...), on the training data or on newdata.

For an lm or glm object the fitted values on the response scale and the stored response are used. The response must be a numeric vector: a logistic glm with a factor or two-column response is refused.

Measures on the training data are optimistic; crossVal() reports the cross-validated root mean squared and mean absolute error.

See also

crossVal() for cross-validated measures, classification-metrics

Other modelling: classification-metrics, fitMod(), logitFirth, plot.FitMod(), predict.FitMod(), predictors(), print.FitMod()

Examples

fit <- fitMod(mpg ~ hp + wt, mtcars, engine = "lm")
mae(fit)
#> [1] 1.901484
rmse(fit)
#> [1] 2.468854
mape(fit)
#> [1] 0.09742983

# a plain lm
rmse(lm(mpg ~ hp + wt, mtcars))
#> [1] 2.468854

# out of sample
set.seed(1)
d <- splitTrainTest(mtcars, p = 0.3)
rmse(update(fit, data = d$train), newdata = d$test)
#> [1] 2.820497
